region.text: Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Limbuwan and the Mechi-Teesta Terai

ledger.note: Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Limbuwan and the Terai between the Mechi and the Teesta are Sikkim's before they are lost (1835 'cession of Darjeeling', 1706 Kalimpong 'said to have come under the control of Bhutan', 1788 'took Limbuana', 1817 'territory annexed by the Nepalese' returned). The History page, in the paragraph after the 1642 consecration, says the first Chogyal 'annexed the Chumbi Valley, the present-day Darjeeling district, and parts of today's eastern Nepal' without a year, so the lands are the page's and the founding year is the bridge (confidence 2, raised from 1 on re-reading). The Chumbi Valley is not drawn (no page opened dates its loss). The Limbuwan page says Limbuwan 'was fully independent until' its 1774 integration into the Gorkha kingdom and does not say Sikkim ruled it, so the Limbuwan disc is the weakest part of the bridge.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-x. A state Cliopatria lacks: cliopatria_names empty, every keyframe new. Four pages opened at first (Kingdom of Sikkim, History of Sikkim, Treaty of Titalia, Treaty of Tumlong) and three more for the repair of 2026-10-25 (Kalimpong, Darjeeling district, Limbuwan; History of Sikkim and the Kingdom page were re-read); WebFetch returned extracts.

Shape: the pages name the Sikkim core and five lost or contested lands: Limbuwan (taken 1788), the Terai between the Mechi and the Teesta (overrun by the Gorkhas before 1814, returned at Titalia on 10 February 1817, annexed with the Darjeeling district in 1861), Darjeeling (the 138-square-mile enclave ceded 1835) and Kalimpong (Bhutanese from 1706). The History page says the first Chogyal 'annexed the Chumbi Valley, the present-day Darjeeling district, and parts of today's eastern Nepal' without a year, so these lands enter at 1642 as a confidence-2 bridge (the lands are the page's, the date is not). The Chumbi Valley (no page dates its loss), Ilam and the Duars are not drawn. The 1861 shape is the Sikkim admin-1: 27 cells, about 6,830 km2 on the grid, against the page's 'over 2,500 square miles (6,500 km2)' for the rump state (ratio 1.05).

Pages disagree: the Kingdom page has Bhutanese invasions in 1680 and 1700 and domination to 1792, the Nepalese invasion in 1776 and domination 1776-1792; the History page has Bhutan in 1700-1706 and the Gorkha invasion in 1788 (used). The Kingdom page lists a ruler list in fragments (Phuntsog Namgyal 1642-1670, Tensung Namgyal from 1670, Palden Thondup Namgyal 1963-1975), so no ruler strip is given. The Kingdom page says the Tibetan protectorate status ended in 1890 (infobox) and the Treaty of Tumlong page that China recognised the British protectorate by the Convention of Calcutta (1890). The History page puts the referendum-era deposition on 9 April 1975 (the Kingdom page says only that the parliament requested statehood).

Page silent: the 1849 Campbell-Hooker affair and the 1850 punitive action are in the History page without a year for the expedition (the Tumlong page names 1861); the Standstill Agreement of 1947 and whether Sikkim was an Indian protectorate between 1947 and December 1950 (the vassal pair is left open for 1947-1950); the Anglo-Nepalese War period of Sikkim as a British ally.

Cross-dossier: east-india-company records the Titalia return (1817) as a loss and the 1835 Darjeeling cession as a gain; the nepal dossier (another part of sa-06) should carry the matching Limbuwan gain of 1788 if its pages support it. Gazetteer: Limbuwan, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Rabdentse and Yuksom are absent from places.jsonl; coordinate circles used (Darjeeling 88.26 E 27.04 N, Kalimpong 88.47 27.06, Limbuwan 87.9 27.2, Terai 88.27 26.9). A Kalimpong place name is needed in the gazetteer (kingdom-of-bhutan uses it too).

REPAIR of 2026-10-25 (reviewer finding: fail). What changed and why:
1. The outlying lands were drawn as circles that overlapped the Sikkim admin-1 itself, so the 1788-1975 keyframes lost half of Sikkim (14-19 of 27 cells) and the capital Tumlong fell outside every keyframe of its years. Every outlying piece is now defined WITHOUT the admin-1 ({minus: [circle, Sikkim]}): Kalimpong = circle minus Sikkim; the Darjeeling hill = circle minus (Sikkim, Kalimpong); Limbuwan and the Terai = circles minus (Sikkim, Darjeeling, Kalimpong). Cell counts on the grid: 1642-1705 84; 1706-1787 81; 1788-1816 28 (Sikkim 27 + the Darjeeling cell); 1817-1834 48 (+ the Terai, 20 cells); 1835-1860 47 (Sikkim + Terai); 1861-1975 27 (the admin-1, equal to the 1975 dissolve region).
2. The Darjeeling disc was 30 km (about 2,800 km2); the Darjeeling district page (re-read) gives 'an enclave of 138 square miles' (357 km2) for the 1835 cession, so the disc is now 10 km (one grid cell, 253 km2). The rest of the district's lower hills fall in the Terai piece. east-india-company uses the same pieces for its 1816, 1817 and 1835 events.
3. Kalimpong (Kalimpong page: ruled in succession by Sikkim and Bhutan; 'said to have come under the control of Bhutan in the year 1706') is now in the 1642 bridge and lost to kingdom-of-bhutan in 1706, mirroring kingdom-of-bhutan /ledger/5 (that dossier's counterpart string is 'sikkim', not this slug; for its owner).
4. The 1861 loss is the Terai only (the hill had gone in 1835); K1 text and the area of the rump state are now consistent (ratio 1.05, no longer 0.54).
Where I disagree or the pages disagree: (a) the reviewer's recipe kept the 30 km Darjeeling disc; the Darjeeling district page's 138 square miles makes it a one-cell enclave, which I used. (b) The Limbuwan page (opened for the thin finding) says Limbuwan was independent until its integration into the Gorkha kingdom in 1774 and says nothing of Sikkim ruling it after the Namgyal dynasty began ('Limbuwan lost the area between Kangchenjunga range and Teesta River' to Sikkim, undated); the History page's 1788 'took Limbuana' is kept (loss at confidence 2) and the 1642 bridge, whose Limbuwan part is the weakest, is at confidence 2 for Darjeeling and Kalimpong but should be read as 1 for Limbuwan. (c) Terai/Darjeeling annexation: the History page says 1861, the Darjeeling district page gives no year for the Terai (it dates the Treaty of Sinchula to November 1864, not 1865), and the 1850 date the reviewer mentions is on no page opened; 1861 stays. (d) The Terai circle (50 km) is wider than the Mechi-Teesta strip (it reaches 87.85 E, west of the Mechi); no page gives the strip's outline, so it stays a circle.

Suzerainty events kept out of the ledger: vassal_start and vassal_end belong in the suzerain's dossier with this state as the counterpart (the schema: 'counterpart is the vassal itself'), so they are listed here for whoever writes or checks the suzerain. 1861-03 vassal_start (suzerain british-raj, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Tumlong): March 1861: the Treaty of Tumlong. Sikkim became 'a de facto protectorate of the British Empire' after the punitive expedition of 1860-61 (Sir Ashley Eden signed; the Chogyal's father refused to return from Tibet); indemnity Rs. 7,000. | 1947 vassal_end (suzerain british-raj, confidence 2, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Sikkim): 1947: Sikkim's guarantees of independence 'were transferred to the Indian government when it gained independence in 1947'. The page does not say whether Sikkim was a protectorate of India before December 1950. | 1950-12 vassal_start (suzerain republic-of-india, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Sikkim): December 1950: 'by signing the India-Sikkim Peace Treaty, Sikkim became India's protectorate.' | 1975-05 vassal_end (suzerain republic-of-india, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Sikkim): 16 May 1975: Sikkim becomes a state of India ('the Indian parliament announced that Sikkim officially became a state of India'); the Sikkim Parliament had deposed the king on 9 April.
